title: Worklflow question
author: DinnerCrazy809
selftext:
Hi all

I've been working on something of a grand strategy/emergent story game but where you play as a criminal who can build his empire through various means, and npcs like rival gangs, cops, business owners are all part of the system with each character having their own personality and goals and actions. I know nothing about coding, I took a C++ course in college and totally forgot everything.  

I started off just shooting ideas to chatgpt, 20$ plan, Influences, what systems should be in place, features, what you can and can't do. Then i had chatgpt make design documents, and then sent those to claude, also 20$, who was fed the ideas and helped build a roadmap. Then i had them share the same project directory, so they are both aware of particular instructions, agents, commits, etc. 

So now at some 26000 lines of code my work flow looks like this 

Claude Fable 5.1- build out the scope of a milestone

Chat GPT Codex Sol 5.6- Review milestone and make recommendations

Claude Sonnet 5.1- code the actual mechanic 

Codex Sol - review code, run tests, provide feedback, feed to Sonnet

Sonnet- takes recommendations, codes again, awaits rereview

Codex- rereviews as needed until milestone is considered complete. 

Do think this is an efficient use of resources and tokens? Anyone else doing something similar?

comments.author: aeturnis-dev
comments.body:
How I operate(I use pro) is with ChatGPT and Claude Code and a remote git repo.

I design with ChatGPT, start the initial project with Claude reading the design document(s) (Invariants, no gos, scopes, out of scopes, milestones, implementation process, models), then initiate the project.

Commit often.

Push at a milestone, have ChatGPT pull the push for adversarial review, iterate again with Claude(And I have Claude create extensive regression and linting test harnesses for my projects).

With the remote repo I also use a dedicated communicated branch for ChatGPT and Claude to "Communicate" with via Handoffs, and I've found that saves a lot of time and potentially Usage between copy+pasting outputs between models, and helps keep things organized.

replies.author: DinnerCrazy809
replies.body: Sounds like we are doing very similar things, I have a remote repo as well, and yes, lots of commits, even for review. I'd like to know how you set up your seperate branch!

replies.author: aeturnis-dev
replies.body: I create a branch called /forum, and I initiate a first forum handoff with Claude for ChatGPT to pull from that branch(And claude pushes the handoff only to the branch) and I usually, if passing to ChatGPT in the flow will say something like "Forum post #0032 pushed to /forum. comments.author: helloimfranky
comments.body:
Www.neoncoastcity.com

Only used Claude opus on medium and Luna on high with thinking on in VScode. I prompted the two to plan things 60% of the time before sending out the actual instruction prompt. I don’t use them at the same time. One task per branch, or one branch per “batched tasks”, which are very closely related tasks.

Also, instead of having the model do things i ask. i have it review and give me suggestions.
